column11: derived: Pfizer generated $23,703mm of free cash flow on $185,759mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 12.76% margin, against the 33.8% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. The 2021 and 2022 COVID years are excluded because a 36% margin on a vaccine windfall is not what this company earns. Restated before interest: PFE paid $8,181mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 4.40% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 22.18% to 17.77%. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Restated without one-off cash: PFE's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $1,350mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $63mm of legal settlements; $4,400mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,000mm; 2024 instalment 1,300mm; 2025 instalment 2,100mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 17.77% to 14.52%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 PFE's cash flow statement shows receivables up $25mm, inventories up $1,462mm, payables down $1,792mm, a working capital build of $3,279mm, 1.77% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 14.52% to 12.66%.

column11: lookup.py demand Padcev: Part B 2024, $641,224,462 over 5,839 beneficiaries = $109,818 per beneficiary
column12: House convention: Padcev (enfortumab vedotin) is the closest marketed comparator. It is an MMAE ADC, and with pembrolizumab it is the 1L la/mUC standard DV+P would compete against. Case against: CMS per-beneficiary spend is a part-year figure. Padcev's 2024 Part B units (18,152,640 of 0.25 mg over 5,839 beneficiaries) are about 777 mg a beneficiary, roughly four 21-day cycles, so a full treated year costs several times this. The house gross-to-net on a Part B price takes off only the 6% ASP add-on (see gross_to_net_pct), so this part-year understatement is not offset; the book accepts that on every Part B-priced seed. A second case against: Enhertu, the marketed HER2 ADC, runs $69,140 per Part B beneficiary in 2024 (lookup.py demand Enhertu), 37% below Padcev. No published annual list price for DV exists, since it is not approved in the US.

column11: Social Security Act section 1847A: Medicare Part B pays 106% of average sales price, and ASP is already net of manufacturer discounts and rebates, so the manufacturer's price is the CMS Part B figure divided by 1.06, 5.66% below it. backend/gross_to_net.py: the 0.5 convention is measured on Part D drugs and 'says nothing about Part B, where ... the deduction there is the 6% add-on and is derived from the statute rather than assumed'. The book carries 0.056604 on the AZD5335 seed the researcher cited, and on Part B-priced ADC seeds such as zilovertamab vedotin, PF-08046054 and sacituzumab tirumotecan
column12: Net is 94.34% of list: 0.109818 x (1 - 0.056604) = 0.103602 mm USD. Direction checked: share OFF list. The price is Padcev's Part B spending per beneficiary, so the Part B convention applies, not the Part D halving. Case against: a Part B per-beneficiary figure is part-year (Padcev's 777 mg a beneficiary is about four cycles), and nothing here offsets that, so revenue per treated patient-year is likely understated; ASP also leaves out 340B and Medicaid prices, which would push net lower

column11: Seagen FY2021 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1060736/000106073622000016/sgen-20211231.htm) and 8-K (0001193125-21-278354): $200mm upfront for exclusive rights outside RemeGen's territory (Asia excluding Japan and Singapore), up to $195mm of development and $2.2bn of regulatory and commercial milestones, and 'a tiered, high single digit to mid-teen percentage royalty based on net sales of disitamab vedotin in Seagen's territory'. Pfizer FY2025 10-K (0000078003-26-000026) footnote (d): 'Disitamab vedotin is being developed in collaboration with RemeGen Co., Ltd.' Netted as the book nets every royalty: the lowest stated tier over Pfizer's pre-tax margin from its company rows (cost of sales 25.67%, SG&A 22.04%, R&D 16.68%, other costs 12.6603%), a 22.9497% margin. (0.229497 - 0.07) / 0.229497 = 0.6950
column12: JUDGEMENT on the tier: 'high single digit' taken at its bottom, 7%, as the litifilimab seed takes 'mid-single-digit' at 4% and the PF-08634404, VLA15 and ralinepag seeds take their lowest stated tier. The engine applies economics_share to the rNPV (forecast.py: owner_rnpv = rnpv x share), not to revenue, so a royalty on sales takes its share of the margin: every cost in the build scales with revenue. Milestones are not netted, as in the other royalty seeds. Case lower: a 12% blended royalty gives 0.4771 and the 15% top tier 0.3464. Case higher: Pfizer's cost of sales already carries an average royalty burden, so netting this one on top double-counts part of it. The PF-08634404 and VLA15 seeds were struck on an earlier 21.09% margin, which would give 0.6681 here

column11: Two filters. (1) About 22,542 US patients a year are diagnosed with or progress to la/mUC, of whom 11,600 receive first-line therapy (Hepp et al., 'Epidemiology and treatment patterns for locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma: a systematic literature review and gap analysis', J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2021;27(2):240, doi:10.18553/jmcp.2020.20285, PMID 33355035); the figure the vepugratinib seed carries. (2) HER2 IHC 1+ or higher, the SGNDV-001 entry criterion: 'In UC, approximately 60% to 80% of patients have tumors that demonstrate HER2 expression' (Powles et al., SGNDV-001 design paper, Future Oncol 2025;21(21):2705, doi:10.1080/14796694.2025.2535280, PMID 40728126), taken at 60%. 11,600 x 0.60 = 6,960 a year, over the book's 84,530 = 0.08234
column12: JUDGEMENT on the HER2 share: the bottom of the trial sponsor's own range; its midpoint, 70%, gives 0.0961. The base is first-line-treated patients, the same denominator as the Flatiron share in penetration_peak_pct, so the two multiply on one basis. Case against, lower: SGNDV-001 enrols only patients eligible for platinum chemotherapy, so a label that follows the trial would leave out platinum-ineligible patients. Case against, higher: the JMCP flow model predates EV+P, which may have raised the share of la/mUC patients who get first-line therapy. Upper-tract tumours sit in neither the 84,530 nor, necessarily, the 11,600

column11: Incumbent: enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab (Padcev plus Keytruda). Flatiron Health, ASCO GU 2026, 'Real-world use and effectiveness of first-line EV+P in advanced urothelial carcinoma in the US' (https://www.urotoday.com/conference-highlights/asco-gu-2026/asco-gu-2026-bladder-cancer/166997-asco-gu-2026-real-world-use-and-effectiveness-of-first-line-enfortumab-vedotin-with-pembrolizumab-in-patients-with-advanced-urothelial-carcinoma-in-the-us.html): 420 of 821 1L patients (51%) received EV+P in 2024, against 15% in 2023. 0.51 x 0.5 = 0.255
column12: JUDGEMENT: half of what the incumbent measurably captured. On an incidence pool this field is the share of each year's eligible starts. SGNDV-001 compares against chemotherapy, not EV+P, and EV+P is already the standard in HER2-expressing patients, so DV must take share from Pfizer's own Padcev rather than from chemotherapy. Case against, lower: no head-to-head against EV+P, and Pfizer impaired DV by $1.6bn in 2025 and $200mm in 2024 on 'updated long-range commercial forecasts' and 'emerging competition' (FY2025 10-K 0000078003-26-000026), which signals modest expectations. Case higher: fewer grade 3 or worse toxicities than chemotherapy and no EV neuropathy or skin toxicity. EV+P reached 62% of first-line starts in 2025 in the same series, so the incumbent's share is still rising. The eligible pool is now first-line-treated patients, the same denominator as this share.
